rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis adds SiC to ZrB2 and sinters at ~1700 °C, whereas the paper uses a ZrB2-AlFeNiCoCr cermet consolidated by SPS at 1300–1600 °C. These are different kinds of interventions (ceramic additive vs. high-entropy-alloy binder).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies reactive sintering in inert atmosphere at ~1700 °C, while the paper uses SPS under vacuum at 1300–1600 °C with a 50 MPa pressure and 5 min hold. The temperature ranges and processing methods differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes an in-situ silica/borosilicate intergranular phase as a diffusion barrier, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on liquid HEA binder fluidity, pore filling, and grain bonding to suppress Al penetration and wear. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance with comparable strength, while the paper measures density, hardness, fracture toughness, molten-Al corrosion rate, and wear volume, finding an optimum at 1500 °C. The predicted property direction (improved corrosion resistance) is general, but the specific property set and comparison differ.
